title: Unlock an Android phone lying loose on a desk by drawing its Z pattern with one fingertip, never lifting it
instruction: Unlock the phone by drawing its pattern with one fingertip, without lifting it: along the top row of dots from left to right, diagonally down to the bottom-left dot, then along the bottom row from left to right. Then take your hand off the phone.
context: Drawing an unlock pattern is something millions of people do many times a day, and a home or care robot handed someone's phone must do it too. Unlike a pinch or a single swipe, it is an ordered path through small targets with two sharp turns, in one unbroken contact: the fingertip must pass within 5.7 mm of each of seven dots in order, keep clear of the two others, and stay pressed on the glass through both corners, because touching a wrong dot or lifting once fails the whole attempt (and five failures lock the phone for 30 s). The phone is loose, so the press and the one-sided drag of a single sliding fingertip must not push it across the desk.
setup: Metres; x forward from the line through the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up from the desk top; arm bases at (0, +0.305) and (0, -0.305). (1) Phone, loose, no case: Google Pixel 7a, 152.0 x 72.9 x 9.0 mm, 193.5 g, glass front, plastic back, lying screen up in portrait, its top pointing away from the robot (+x), centred at (0.235, -0.135) on a laminate desk. Screen 63.6 x 141.3 mm (6.1 in, 20:9), awake, showing the lock screen's pattern pad (woken and swiped up before the trial): a clock above, nine 2.2 mm dots in a 3 x 3 grid at 19 mm pitch centred 30 mm below the screen centre (estimate). The stored pattern is a Z: top row left to right, the diagonal to the bottom-left dot, bottom row left to right (dots 1-2-3-5-7-8-9, numbered from the top left, row by row). Settings: Make pattern visible on, screen timeout 10 min, airplane mode, a test phone whose pattern is this Z. (2) Robot fingertip: the right gripper's two end faces (each about 15 x 4 mm) closed together and wrapped in conductive fabric tape grounded to the robot frame; in simulation a face touches when it rests on the glass (within 0.2 mm). Nothing else on the desk. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. Dots are 0.24-0.29 m from the right arm base.
scoring: Read from the phone (in the real trial: its screen and the overhead video, where Make pattern visible shows the drawn line; lifting submits a pattern). LEAD of an attempt: how many of its dots match the pattern from the start, counting the one still being drawn. Score 0 if the phone turned over (tilted over 45 degrees) or left the desk (20 mm below it). Otherwise the lower of two numbers. Screen: 1.0 unlocked with no earlier attempt; 0.75 unlocked after any earlier attempt (wrong dot, too short or lifted early); 0.5 not unlocked and some attempt has LEAD 4-7; 0.25 best LEAD 1-3; 0 no attempt began on the first dot (includes doing nothing). Phone: 1.0 centre within 20 mm of its start, turned at most 10 degrees, and for 1 s every fingertip 20 mm or more above the glass or 10 mm outside the phone, phone still; 0.75 in place but the hand not yet off; 0.5 moved more than 20 mm or turned more than 10 degrees. Success: 1.0 held 1 s more.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (60 s at 20 Hz), about 2.5x the scripted demo's 23.8 s
reset_notes: Wait for the screen to go back to the pattern pad (a wrong pattern clears after 2 s); if the phone unlocked, press the power button twice to lock and wake it and swipe up to show the pattern pad. After five failed attempts (4 or more dots) the phone shows a 30 s wait: let it run out before the next trial. Lay the phone back on its tape outline, top away from the robot; ready pose, grippers open. About 30-60 s a trial.
fidelity: Pattern rules ported from Android 14's open-source LockPatternView (hit radius 0.3 x pitch, gap fill, used dots, under 4 dots refused, 5 tries then 30 s). Pad position and 19 mm pitch are estimates from Android's layout values. Touch is a face on the glass within 0.2 mm, not capacitive sensing; no panel filtering or haptics; read at 20 Hz, filled in every 1 mm. Phone one rigid body, friction 0.4/0.35 (estimate); camera bar not modelled.
